digest.top_line: RT CHARM: PMRT at 42.56 Gy/16 fx noninferior to 50 Gy/25 fx for 24-mo reconstruction complications, 12.3% vs 10.2%, difference -2.1% (95% CI -6.5 to 2.2).
digest.tldr: Single-site day carried by breast: RT CHARM supports moderate hypofractionation for PMRT with reconstruction, with 3-yr local/LR RFS 97.0% vs 96.2% (HR 1.01) and less G2 dermatitis (20% vs 42%). Caveats: wide 10% NI margin, median f/u 3.9 yr, underpowered reconstruction subgroups. Delayed reconstruction predicted complications (OR 2.96).

verdict.rationale: Randomized NI met across 209 sites with low LRR; wide 10% absolute margin against a 10.2% control rate and 3.9-yr f/u keep it short of practice-changing.
verdict.audience: Post-mastectomy, T0-3 N0-2a M0, immediate or delayed reconstruction

studies.significance: Reconstruction timing mattered more than fractionation: delayed reconstruction carried OR 2.96 for complications in either arm, while arm was not a predictor. LRR at 3 yr was 1.5% vs 2.2% and G2 dermatitis halved (20% vs 42%), so this supports 16 fx PMRT for reconstructed pts, including implant-only.
studies.monday_clinic: In a woman needing PMRT for T0-3 N0-2a disease with immediate or planned delayed reconstruction, implant or autologous, this supports 16-fraction PMRT over 25 fractions; it does not extend to T4, N3, positive margins or prior thoracic RT.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Unblinded 2-arm randomized noninferiority trial**, 1:1, 209 US and Canadian sites, enrolled 2018-2021. **N=898 enrolled, 825 evaluable** (38 withdrew before RT, 35 ineligible). Median f/u 3.9 yr.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **T0N1-2a, T1N1-2a, T2N1-2a or T3N0-2a, M0** after mastectomy, ECOG 0-1, with completed, ongoing or intended reconstruction. Excluded T4, N3, positive margins, collagen vascular disease, bilateral or prior ipsilateral cancer, prior thoracic RT. Median age 49, N1 76%, 51% neoadjuvant chemo.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50 Gy/25 fx over 5 wk vs 42.56 Gy/16 fx over 3 wk.** IROC plan QA: 90% per-protocol or acceptable, 4% unacceptable. Target volumes and boost not stated in source excerpt.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** composite reconstruction complications at 24 mo (wound healing, readmission, capsular contracture, unplanned reoperation, failure). NI margin **10%**. Secondary: local/locoregional recurrence, acute and late toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: NI met in ITT and in the 631 pts who completed reconstruction within 18 mo. Fractionation effect did not appear to differ by reconstruction type or timing.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Acute G3+ non-reconstruction toxicity 5.0% vs 7.7% (p=0.11). RT-attributed toxicity similar except **dermatitis, less frequent with hypofractionation**. Late toxicity not statistically different.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Extends the hypofractionation evidence from post-lumpectomy trials (START, FAST-Forward) and post-mastectomy without reconstruction to the reconstructed chest wall, the setting where adoption lagged. Sits alongside FABREC, which tested the same 16-fraction schedule in implant reconstruction; RT CHARM adds autologous and delayed reconstructions.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents women needing PMRT for T0-3 N0-2a M0 disease with immediate or delayed, implant or autologous reconstruction. Does not represent T4, N3, positive-margin or previously irradiated chest walls.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Margin of 10% was powered on an assumed 25% control rate, but control ran 10.2%, so the margin is relatively generous. Unblinded assessment of complications; 35 pts lacked reconstruction forms at freeze. Late contracture and failure need longer f/u.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Reconstruction timing (delayed OR 2.96) moved complication risk far more than fractionation. The remaining questions are long-term reconstruction durability and whether shorter schedules (5 fx) hold up in this setting.

studies.interpretation:
The reason this trial needed to exist is not oncologic. Hypofractionation was settled for the conserved breast years ago through START and FAST-Forward, and post-mastectomy hypofractionation without reconstruction had its own supporting data, yet many practices kept reconstructed pts on 25 fractions because the reconstruction was the perceived fragile structure. RT CHARM answers that worry directly, with a reconstruction-specific primary endpoint, across 209 academic and community sites, and with every reconstruction type and sequence allowed. That pragmatic eligibility is the main source of its external validity: this is the mix of implants, expanders, autologous flaps and delayed sequences that actually arrives in clinic. It sits next to FABREC, which addressed the same 16-fraction schedule in implant reconstruction; the added value here is the autologous and delayed cohorts and the stratification on them.

The noninferiority framing deserves a careful read. The 10% absolute margin was set against an assumed 25% control complication rate, but the control arm ran at 10.2%. Against that baseline, a 10-point margin would have tolerated roughly a doubling of complications, which is a generous threshold. The upper bound of the observed interval (6.5 points on the stated scale) is what a skeptic should anchor on, rather than the noninferiority p-value. Even so, the point estimate difference of 2.1 points is small, the completed-reconstruction analysis of 631 pts gave a consistent -2.2% with an interval reaching 7.2, and the multivariable model found arm was not a predictor. Read together, the data argue that any fractionation penalty, if real, is modest and much smaller than the effect of reconstruction timing.

That timing signal is the most decision-relevant finding for the multidisciplinary team. Delayed reconstruction carried an OR of 2.96 for complications regardless of arm, while implant-only versus autologous (OR 1.65, p=0.07) did not reach significance despite the abstract's wording. Because timing was a stratification factor rather than a randomized comparison, this is an association within a randomized cohort, confounded by why reconstruction was delayed (expander strategy, neoadjuvant course, surgeon preference). It should inform counselling, not be read as evidence that immediate reconstruction is safer.

Oncologically, 3-yr locoregional recurrence was low in both arms, 1.5% versus 2.2%, with an LRRFS HR of 1.01 and an interval spanning 0.53 to 1.96. With 18 total events the trial cannot exclude a modest LRR difference, and it was never powered to; the reassurance comes from consistency with the broader hypofractionation literature rather than from this trial alone. The acute toxicity gain is real and patient-visible, with G2 dermatitis falling from 42% to 20%.

What would make the conclusion wrong? Late reconstruction events, capsular contracture in particular, can emerge beyond 3 to 4 years, and a hypofractionation penalty on late tissue effects would surface there first. Unblinded complication assessment could bias in either direction. Finally, target volumes, internal mammary coverage, bolus and boost practice are not described in the source excerpt, so transfer to a given nodal-coverage policy assumes comparable planning. The practical read is that fear of reconstruction failure is no longer a sound reason to withhold 16-fraction PMRT, while 5-fraction schedules in this setting remain untested here.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Supports 42.56 Gy/16 fx PMRT with reconstruction in place or planned: complications noninferior, 3-yr LRR 1.5% vs 2.2%, G2 dermatitis 20% vs 42%. Target volumes and boost use are not in the source excerpt, so nodal-coverage transferability still needs the full protocol.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Reconstruction timing, not RT schedule, drove complications: delayed vs immediate OR 2.96 (1.4-6.2) regardless of arm. Implant-only trended higher (OR 1.65, p=0.07). Fear of hypofractionation should no longer shape reconstruction type or timing choices.

papers.title: Randomized Trial of Hypofractionated Postmastectomy Radiation Therapy in Women With Breast Reconstruction (RT CHARM, Alliance A221505).
papers.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with breast cancer requiring postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) often desire breast reconstruction. Reconstructions can be adversely affected by PMRT, and fear of reconstruction complications has discouraged adoption of short-course radiation therapy used after lumpectomy. To fill the evidence gap, we conducted a noninferiority trial of hypofractionated versus conventional PMRT in patients undergoing breast reconstruction. The primary outcome was reconstruction complication rate, a composite of wound healing, readmission, capsular contracture, unplanned reoperation, and reconstruction failure.

METHODS: Women with unilateral invasive breast cancer with planned immediate or delayed reconstruction and PMRT were randomly assigned (1:1) to 50 Gy (25 fractions/5 weeks) or 42.56 Gy (16 fractions/3 weeks). This study was designed with a noninferiority margin of 10%, assuming a 2-year reconstruction complication rate of 25% with conventional PMRT. Randomization was stratified by immediate versus delayed and autologous versus implant-only reconstruction.

RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2021, 898 patients enrolled with a median follow-up of 3.9 years; 825 patients were evaluable for the primary end point. The 24-month reconstruction complication rates were 12.3% (52/422) with hypofractionated PMRT and 10.2% (41/403) with conventional PMRT, corresponding to an estimated difference of -2.1% (95% CI, -6.5 to 2.2). The complication rate was higher (regardless of arm) with implant-only versus autologous reconstruction (odds ratio = 1.65). There was no statistically significant difference in 36-month locoregional recurrence rates: 1.5% (95% CI, 0.7 to 3.2) with hypofractionated and 2.2% (95% CI, 1.1 to 4.3) with conventional PMRT. Acute and late toxicity rates were not statistically different.

CONCLUSION: A 16-fraction course of hypofractionated PMRT is safe and noninferior to conventional PMRT in women undergoing breast reconstruction after mastectomy.
